description: Retrieval evaluation for document RAG (ADR-0015). Passages are chunks of one fictional annual report. Each question names the passage that answers it, or null when the report does not answer it. Answerable questions paraphrase their passage rather than repeating its words, so they test meaning, not keyword overlap. 'near_miss' questions sound like the report but are not answered by it: the hard case for the relevance floor.

passages.text: Total revenue for fiscal 2025 reached $48.2 million, up 12% from the prior year. Growth came mainly from enterprise subscriptions, which rose 19%, while one-off consulting revenue declined.
Operating expenses fell 3% to $39.5 million. The largest saving came from consolidating two data centres into one, partly offset by higher spending on cloud hosting.
Headcount grew from 310 to 356 employees. Most new hires joined engineering and customer success; the sales team stayed the same size.
In March we launched Northwind Insights, an analytics add-on priced at $15 per user per month. By year end it had been adopted by 140 customers.

On 14 August an attacker used a stolen contractor credential to access a staging server. No customer data was exposed. We rotated all credentials and now require hardware security keys for contractors.
The London team moved to a smaller office in Shoreditch in June, reducing rent by roughly a third. Staff now work in the office three days a week.
Our data centre now runs on 85% renewable electricity, and total carbon emissions fell 22% compared with 2024. We aim for net zero operations by 2030.
Median first response time for support tickets improved from 6 hours to 2.5 hours after we introduced a follow-the-sun rota across three time zones.
A former distributor sued the company for breach of contract in the Delaware courts. We believe the claim is without merit; no provision has been recorded.
Research and development spending was $9.1 million, about 19% of revenue, focused on the query engine rewrite and on machine-learning forecasting features.
The board proposes a final dividend of 4 pence per share, payable on 30 April to shareholders on the register on 1 April.
The principal risks are dependence on two large customers, which together account for 27% of revenue, and the possibility of a prolonged cloud provider outage.
